To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the "complex-as-metal/complex-as-ligands" strategy is a very efficient synthetic route for the preparation of heterotrinuclear oxalato-bridge Cr(III)-Co(II) complexes.
the magnetic coupling in oxalato-based trinuclear Cr(III)-Co(II) complexes can be controlled by varying the aromatic diimines used as terminal ligands and the magnetic anisotropies of the metal ions.
we have designed and synthesized two novel heterotrinolecular chromium(III)- cobalt(II)-based complexes with the "complex-as-metal" approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of new molecular materials based on oxalato-bridge heterotrinuclear complexes with the aim to obtain a detailed insight into the magnetic properties of these systems.
the design of novel oxalato- and carboxylato-bridged heterotrinuclear complexes exhibiting weak but non-neglible intermolecular magnetic coupling and single-ion anisotropy.
the synthesis, structural characterization, and magnetic properties of two novel oxalato- and diimine-based heterotrinuclear Cr(III)(bipyridine)(2)Co(bipyridine)(Me(2)) complexes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the "complex-as-metal/complex-as-ligands" strategy is a very powerful tool to synthesize novel heterometallic complexes with unusual structural motifs.

the oxalato- and diimine-based ligand framework in 1 and/or 2 is a very efficient structural and functional unit for the construction of heterochiral oxalato-bridge-based trinuclear Cr(III)CoII complexes possessing weak intermolecular antiferrromagnetic coupling, which is a consequence of the moderate ferromagnetic coupling across the oxalate bridge as well as of the single-ion magnetic anisotropies of the central cobalt(II

the oxalato-bridge in these heterotrinuclear complexes is not an ideal bridge to achieve ferromagnetic coupling between chromium(III) and cobalt(II), but the presence of a weak antiferromagnetic coupling is observed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the oxalato-bridge is not only an excellent bridging ligand but also an excellent template for the design and construction of novel molecular magnetic materials.

oxalato-bridge heterotrimers of the general formula [Mn(III)(2)Ln(II)](n) are not always ferromagnetically coupled, and the presence of a magnetic anisotropic metal ion (e.g., Co(II)) in a trimeric structure may lead to a significant single-ion anisotropy contribution to the magnetic behavior.

the oxalato-bridge in 1 and/or 2 does not favor ferromagnetic coupling, as it is often assumed, and that the ferromagnetic exchange interaction in 2 is the strongest one observed for a Cr(III)(3)Co(II), Cr(III)(4)Co(II)/Co(III), or Cr(III)(5)Co(II/III) heterotrimetallic complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the "complex-as-metal" approach is not limited to only simple metal ions such as Cu(II), Ni(II), and Co(II), but can be extended to more complex metal ions such as Cr(III) and Co(II).
the "complex-as-metal/complex-as-ligands" strategy is a very powerful synthetic tool to prepare heterotrinuclear complexes possessing a high-spin ground state and appreciable magnetic anisotropies.
weak ferromagnetic exchange interactions between the two Cr(III) ions and the high-spin Co(2+) ion are possible in oxalato-based Cr(III)(n)Co(II)m complexes.
